question: Does a neutral, stable sensory cue for object identity let the unmodified recurrent motor select an informative revisit? The main native motor often treats the displayed half-odor as an appetitive choice.
scene: Each fresh object has a random neutral three-component cue and a separate antipodal food-odor axis. Ordinary left and right sensing is cue*0.8 plus/minus food_vector*orientation; the common cue itself does not determine the rewarding side. Cues, food directions and private signs are regenerated for every life. Study contacts, coverage, real tastes and recurrent time are matched. Review identifies a pair of physically available objects; selecting a side takes a new actual food contact with that object's original common cue and value law.
arms: On the route-only menu display either (tag) each object's own neutral cue, (flavor) one signed food direction at the same amplitude, or (unbound) a fresh neutral cue that was not paired to the study object. Same birth graphs, native two motor nodes, parameters, updates, mode cue, clocks, number of reviews and final actual action. The stable common cue is available on the ordinary studies in all three conditions. Compare matched and randomized private-history action donations to distinguish learning which object needs extra evidence from recognizing scene geometry.
training: Start all arms on both previous six-birth uniform 8k cohorts. 8000 Adam steps with lr=.002. All existing weights, bias and local rules externally trainable, fast numerical and structural editing stays open. 2/4 objects alternate. Three quarters of training geometries have one of two candidates' prior contact yield no taste, crossed on which candidate. Rest have ordinary tastes. A random one of the two offered items is actually queried, score its physically chosen food. No signal to the actor of the hidden assignment, missing object ID, or correct study route.
evaluation: New world seeds 3719451 and 3719467, active and both-observed histories, 2/4/8 object loads, candidate sign versus stable cue masking/swapping at the review menu only. Primary examined on four with missing taste; report native versus uniform both-candidate accuracy, chosen missing rate and whether the very same public menu yields appropriate differences after exchanging which private experience was missing. Compare to matched root-specific benchmarks; transfer to untagged ordinary short recall assessed separately.
